intervals.label: Homestake gold mine
intervals.note: Predecessor operation on the same site; the mine closed before the laboratory was created. The source states the mine operated "from 1876", but 1876 is outside the atlas's supported date range ([1900, 2100], A12); `start` is left null rather than recorded as an out-of-range or substituted value.
intervals.quote: SURF is indelibly linked to the history of the Homestake Mine, which operated from 1876 until 2001.

intervals.label: South Dakota Science and Technology Authority formed
intervals.note: Creation of the operating authority; no end date.
intervals.quote: In 2004, then-Governor Mike Rounds and the State Legislature formed the South Dakota Science and Technology Authority

intervals.label: operating as an underground laboratory
intervals.quote: The Sanford Underground Research Facility (SURF) has been operating since 2007 supporting underground research in rare-process physics

intervals.label: 4850 Level dedicated
intervals.note: Dedication of the 4850 Level after dewatering; treated as a commissioning event with year precision.
intervals.quote: After an extensive dewatering process, the 4850 Level of SURF was dedicated in 2009.

depth.display: 1478 m (4850-foot level); sources round this to about 1500 m
depth.locator: page 'The MAJORANA Demonstrator Project at the 4850 Level Davis Campus', paragraph on the shield and the underground location (the page states the level and its metric value)
depth.note: The 4850 Level is named for its depth in feet: 4850 ft x 0.3048 m/ft = 1478.3 m, the figure SURF itself gives ('4850 Level (1478 m)') and the one the local map uses. SURF's scientific director rounds it to 1500 m in the Snowmass 2022 paper ("campuses at the 4850-foot level (1500 m, 4300 m.w.e.)"); the same author gives 1490 m in a 2024 paper, and DUNE TDR Vol. I says "approximately 1.5 km underground". The water-equivalent overburden is the separate 4300 m.w.e. value. CHANGED 2026-10-25: was value 1500 m, display "1500 m (4850-foot level)" (the Snowmass 2022 rounding), which disagreed with the 1478 m of the map level. Placement of the DUNE far detector at this level: DUNE TDR Vol. I, §1.1.2 and Fig. 1.4 (arXiv PDF p. 25): "the SURF underground area, also referred to as the 4850 (foot) level or 4850L"; ProtoDUNE-SP paper (arXiv:2007.06722, PDF p. 12): "a far detector located at the 4850 ft level of Sanford Underground Research Facility (SURF)". The quote above is SURF's statement for the 4850 Level itself.
depth.quote: The entire experiment will be located at the 4850 Level (1478 m) Davis Campus at the Sanford Lab Underground Research Facility (SURF).

overburden.quote: campuses at the 4850-foot level (1500 m, 4300 m.w.e.)

summary.plain: A laboratory built in a former gold mine in Lead, South Dakota. Nearly a mile of rock above it blocks cosmic rays, so experiments there can look for very rare events, including the giant DUNE neutrino detectors.
summary.technical: Underground laboratory operated by the South Dakota Science and Technology Authority in the former Homestake mine. The 4850-foot level (4850 ft = 1478 m below the surface, rounded to 1500 m in some sources; 4300 m.w.e.) hosts LZ, the Majorana Demonstrator, CASPAR and the LBNF/DUNE far-detector campus.
